messages:
Alex M.: Thanks for the infra update earlier. Quick follow-ups from the all-hands: 1) concrete APAC GPU availability timeline? 2) how are autoscale exceptions handled for Dedicated vs Hosted pools? 3) if supply hits cap, what's the prioritized fallback order?
Priya S.: APAC update — still dependent on vendor ETA but target is late May for initial capacity in apac-syd. procurement will confirm exact ship windows next week. not a hard date yet. :folded_hands:
Matt R.: Autoscale exceptions: current policy is to prevent Hosted autoscaler from spilling into Dedicated pools. we're prototyping an exception rule to allow dedicated->spot-burst but only with throttled qps. testing this week.
Samir K.: Can you clarify when that exception would kick in? We saw one customer hit an unexpected cap last month and it caused retries.
Matt R.: The rule is: if queued time > 300ms and available capacity in fallback zones > 5 nodes then allow burst. otherwise deny. still tuning numbers.
Jordan L.: Working on console support so teams can opt their routes into the canary/exception group. plan is a simple flag: `canary: true` in route config. ETA Tue.
Alex M.: Can you paste a sample config for that?
Jordan L.: Sure —
```
routes:
  - name: realtime
    model: gpt-redwood-v2
    canary: true
    autoscale:
      allow_burst_to_spot: true
    fallback_priority:
      - region: us-west
      - region: apac-syd
```
Priya S.: Action: I'll publish a short runbook for oncall/SEs describing the new exception behavior + fallback priority. Owner: Priya. Due: Fri EOD.
Samir K.: Also: we've seen two burst events where prefix cache invalidation triggered QPS spikes. any planned mitigations?
Matt R.: We're adding a prewarm hook during canary rollout and exploring more persistent KV cache across restarts. that'll reduce those cold-start spikes.
Alex M.: What about SLOs? If we route to fallback regions, customers should know latency may change.
Matt R.: Good call — fallback latency SLO will be documented as a separate bucket (e.g., 250ms target for primary, 350ms for fallback) and we'll surface a banner in Console for routes currently using fallbacks. I'll take on the banner.
Jordan L.: I'll add a `fallback-rate` metric to the per-route dashboard so PMs can see how often routing falls back.
Priya S.: TL;DR action items posted here for visibility:
- Post runbook describing autoscale exceptions & fallback order (Owner: Priya S., due Fri)
- Add console flag + UI for canary/exception routing (Owner: Jordan L., ETA Tue)
- Add fallback SLO doc + console banner (Owner: Matt R., follow-up ticket)
- Implement prewarm hook + KV persistence investigation (Owner: Samir K.)
- Product to draft a customer-facing note for planned APAC availability and potential fallback behavior (Owner: Product)
Alex M.: Thanks — can we have a short sync next week to confirm runbook and banner wording before publish?
Priya S.: Yep. scheduling a 30m sync, invite going out in a bit.
Samir K.: :thumbsup:
Matt R.: I'll open the infra tickets now and link them in this thread.
Jordan L.: PR link when ready: https://git.redwood.local/repos/infra/merge_requests/1234 (will post when I open it)
OpsBot: Ticket INF-879 created by Priya S. (autoscale-exception-runbook)
Alex M.: Great — appreciate the quick follow-ups.
